proposals.title: Gaia v29.1.0 upgrade
proposals.summary:
# Overview

This proposal schedules a coordinated upgrade of the Cosmos Hub to Gaia `v29.1.0`.

**If the proposal passes, validators will be required to update the Cosmos Hub binary at the specified upgrade height.**

**This upgrade is state-breaking.**

## Highlights

- Restore decoding of historical `ParameterChangeProposal` content, fixing governance proposal list, status-filtered, single-proposal and tally queries, as well as state export.
- Update CosmWasm `wasmd` from `v0.60.9` to `v0.60.10`.
- Update CosmWasm `wasmvm` from `v2.3.5` to `v2.3.6`.

### State-Breaking Changes

- Legacy `ParameterChangeProposal` submissions now decode and reach ante processing before governance rejects their execution. As a result, fees and account sequences change for such submissions.

## Release Details

- [Gaia v29.1.0 release](https://github.com/cosmos/gaia/releases#release-v29.1.0)
- [Changelog](https://github.com/cosmos/gaia/blob/v29.1.0/CHANGELOG.md)
- [Upgrading guide](https://github.com/cosmos/gaia/blob/v29.1.0/UPGRADING.md)

# Upgrade Instructions and Verification

Please check the announcements in the established communication channels for release details and upgrade instructions.

Public verification keys and instructions for verifying Gaia release signatures are available in the [official Gaia release signing directory](https://github.com/cosmos/security/tree/main/release/gaia/signing).

# Voting

This proposal has a voting period of **SEVEN DAYS**.

The following items summarize the voting options and what they mean for this proposal:

YES - You agree that the Cosmos Hub should be updated with this release.

NO - You disagree that the Cosmos Hub should be updated with this release.

NO WITH VETO - A `NoWithVeto` vote indicates that the proposal either (1) is deemed to be spam, i.e., irrelevant to Cosmos Hub, (2) disproportionately infringes on minority interests, or (3) violates or encourages violation of the rules of engagement as currently set out by Cosmos Hub governance. Veto thresholds and any deposit burning are governed by the chain's active governance parameters.

ABSTAIN - You wish to contribute to the quorum but formally decline to vote either for or against the proposal.

proposals.metadata: Migrate Community Pool USDC.n to USDC.inj via a Community Multisig
proposals.title: Migrate Community Pool USDC.n to USDC.inj via a Community Multisig
proposals.summary:
## Summary

The Cosmos Hub community pool holds 566,067.055810 USDC.n (Noble-issued USDC). Circle pauses the Noble USDC contract and all Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP) routes to and from Noble on January 12, 2027.

This proposal sends the full USDC.n balance of the community pool to a 4-of-6 DAODAO multisig composed of six Cosmos community members and validators to migrate to USDC.inj (Injective-issued USDC). The multisig will migrate the funds to USDC.inj and return the USDC.inj to the community pool. The multisig holds the funds for the duration of the migration only and has no other mandate.

## Background

On September 10, 2026, Circle announced that it is [discontinuing support for USDC and CCTP V1 on Noble](https://www.circle.com/blog/circle-is-discontinuing-support-for-usdc-and-cctp-v1-on-noble) as part of its transition to CCTP V2. Noble will not receive CCTP V2.

The wind-down runs on the following schedule:

* October 13, 2026: New minting of USDC on Noble through Circle Mint is disabled.

* October 31, 2026: CCTP V1 burn limits from Noble begin reducing gradually to zero.

* January 12, 2027: The Noble USDC contract and all CCTP routes to and from Noble are paused. Circle snapshots remaining Noble USDC balances on this date.

* January 13, 2027: Circle opens a manual redemption process for holders included in the snapshot.

The Cosmos ecosystem is treating USDC.inj as the canonical USDC going forward. Cosmos Labs, Circle, Injective, Skip, and chain teams across the ecosystem coordinated a migration path from USDC.n to USDC.inj that went live on Skip:Go on September 11, 2026. The Cosmos Hub, dYdX, Osmosis, Terra, Neutron, Agoric, ZIGChain, XPLA, and Initia are supported migration origins as of right now, and these chains and more are migrating their own USDC.n liquidity and treasury balances ahead of the deadline.

The Cosmos Hub community pool holds 566,067.055810 USDC.n. The community pool cannot execute a migration transaction on its own, so moving these funds requires a governance-approved spend to an account that can sign the migration and return the proceeds.

## About USDC.inj

USDC on Injective is natively issued by Circle. Circle [launched native USDC and CCTP on Injective](https://www.circle.com/blog/now-available-native-usdc-cctp-on-injective) on May 7, 2026. USDC.inj is backed 1:1 by US dollar reserves held by Circle, carries no bridge or wrapper, and supports CCTP V2 for transfers between Injective and other CCTP chains.

USDC.inj implements Injective's MultiVM Token Standard, so a single balance is accessible from both the Injective EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) and the Cosmos bank module without bridging. It transfers over IBC to any chain with an open Injective channel.

Key identifiers:

* Issuer: Circle (native issuance on Injective)

* Token contract on Injective (EVM): 0xa00C59fF5a080D2b954d0c75e46E22a0c371235a

* Bank denom on Injective: erc20:0xa00C59fF5a080D2b954d0c75e46E22a0c371235a

* Decimals: 6

* CCTP domain ID for Injective: 29

* CCTP V2 TokenMessengerV2 on Injective: 0x28b5a0e9C621a5BadaA536219b3a228C8168cf5d

* CCTP V2 MessageTransmitterV2 on Injective: 0x81D40F21F12A8F0E3252Bccb954D722d4c464B64

* IBC denom on the Cosmos Hub (transfer/channel-220 from Injective): ibc/E107DB3E8AABB49C87CB737A1ABBFDBA9803ECAE05E295D8D7A0B1A7FE83706C

* Chain registry symbol: USDC.inj

For comparison, the USDC.n denom on the Cosmos Hub (transfer/channel-536 from Noble) is ibc/F663521BF1836B00F5F177680F74BFB9A8B5654A694D0D2BC249E03CF2509013.

Reference documentation: [Injective USDC documentation](https://docs.injective.network/developers-defi/usdc-stablecoin), [Circle USDC contract addresses](https://developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses), [Cosmos Hub assetlist entry for USDC.inj](https://github.com/cosmos/chain-registry/blob/master/cosmoshub/assetlist.json).

## Proposal Details

This is a community pool spend proposal (MsgCommunityPoolSpend). If it passes, the full USDC.n balance of the community pool is transferred to a DAODAO multisig on the Cosmos Hub, which executes the migration and returns the proceeds.

### Spend

* Amount: 566,067.055810 USDC.n (566067055810 ibc/F663521BF1836B00F5F177680F74BFB9A8B5654A694D0D2BC249E03CF2509013)
* Recipient: DAODAO multisig on the Cosmos Hub, address cosmos1amny2nf23uauu79lzp299tvh9v4a62uuxvh8xyj7qavrm0adztsq5sz864. You can see the DAO's webpage on DAODAO here: https://daodao.zone/dao/cosmos1amny2nf23uauu79lzp299tvh9v4a62uuxvh8xyj7qavrm0adztsq5sz864/proposals

### Multisig

The recipient is a 4 of 6 DAODAO multisig with the address cosmos1amny2nf23uauu79lzp299tvh9v4a62uuxvh8xyj7qavrm0adztsq5sz864. Any four of the following six members must approve each transaction:

* [Arlai (Hydro)](https://forum.cosmos.network/u/arlai-mk/summary)

* [Johnny Wyles (Osmosis)](https://forum.cosmos.network/u/johnnywyles/summary)

* [Lexa Michaelides (Hypha)](https://forum.cosmos.network/u/lexa/summary)

* [Polkachu](https://forum.cosmos.network/u/polkachu/summary)

* [David (Crosnest)](https://forum.cosmos.network/u/david_crosnest/summary)

* [Zoltan (Silk Nodes)](https://forum.cosmos.network/u/zoltanatom/summary)

The multisig has one mandate: migrate the received USDC.n to USDC.inj and return it to the community pool. It holds no other assets and takes no other action.

### Execution steps

1. Governance passes and the spend executes, delivering 566,067.055810 USDC.n to the multisig.

2. The multisig runs a test migration of a small amount through Skip:Go or the Osmosis USDC transmuter pool, and confirms the USDC.inj arrives in the multisig on the Hub.

3. The multisig migrates the remaining balance through the same route. Receiving the full 566,067.055810 USDC.inj balance in the multisig.

4. The multisig returns the full USDC.inj balance to the community pool with MsgFundCommunityPool.

5. The multisig publishes the transaction hashes for each step in this forum thread once the migration is complete.

Migration proceeds are 1:1. The only costs are gas on the Cosmos Hub, and any relayer fee charged by the Skip:Go route, which is deducted from the migrated amount and is a small fixed fee per transfer rather than a percentage.

### Contingencies

* The multisig may elect to migrate in smaller amounts using Osmosis’s USDC transmuter pool (which also carries no swap fees nor price impact / slippage) depending on what is operationally simpler. Both routes carry essentially identical costs.

* If a migration transaction stalls at any leg, the Skip relayer completes it or the funds remain in the multisig.

* If for any reason the migration cannot be completed, the multisig returns the unmigrated USDC.n to the community pool.

## Timeline

* Tuesday, Oct 20, 2026: Forum discussion period (1 week).

* Tuesday Oct 27, 2026: Target on-chain date

* 7 days from submission: Voting period (the Cosmos Hub voting period is 7 days).

* Within 7 days of the proposal passing: Test migration, full migration, and return of USDC.inj to the community pool. The migration itself completes in minutes or less once the multisig has signed.

## Vote Options

* YES: Send the community pool's USDC.n balance to the 4 of 6 community multisig for migration to USDC.inj and return to the community pool.

* NO: You disagree with sending the community pool's USDC.n balance to the 4 of 6 community multisig for migration to USDC.inj and return to the community pool.

* NO WITH VETO: You consider this proposal spam, harmful to a minority of interests, or in violation of governance rules. A NoWithVeto vote burns the deposit if 33.4% of voting power selects it.

* ABSTAIN: You wish to contribute to quorum without voting for or against.

proposals.title: Move the 1,227,121 ATOM recovered after the Neutron exploit to the Neutron recovery multisig
proposals.summary:
# Move the 1,227,121 ATOM recovered after the Neutron exploit to the Neutron recovery multisig

This is a text proposal. It executes no messages, spends nothing from the community pool and changes no Hub parameter.

If it passes, the Cosmos Hub authorizes the signers of the Hub recovery multisig, `cosmos1z8pq5cn7tdrwwzlwm0e44fgq07e43ner6vph64`, to send its full ATOM balance, less network fees, over IBC to the Neutron recovery multisig, `neutron1yr29fd7uzdjp2jsq8hrta8mvyd6ex7vumn0shy`. A subsequent Neutron governance proposal will then return all recovered funds, including this ATOM, to the original Neutron contracts they were taken from.

## Background

On 22 September 2026 an attacker passed Neutron governance proposal 9 with stake bought for about 20,199 USDC. The proposal handed 11 Neutron contracts to the attacker, who replaced their code, emptied them and bridged the proceeds to other chains. All 1,723,180.290498 ATOM taken went to the attacker's Hub address, `cosmos1dd25c4sshelrpfs0433apg24c5phrhk8m96c4n`. It came from three Neutron contracts, where it was held for Drop and Astroport users:

- Drop dATOM to ATOM converter: 1,589,711.919394 ATOM
- Drop withdrawal manager: 115,878.183542 ATOM
- Astroport ATOM/dATOM pool: 17,590.187562 ATOM

Hub validators halted the chain at block 33,086,740. On 23 September the Hub restarted on Gaia v28.3.0 with a one-time state change at height 33,086,741 that moved the 1,227,121.374688 ATOM still on the attacker's address to a 4-of-6 recovery multisig. No other account, balance or delegation was touched. The signers are Nansen, Keplr, Enigma, Silknodes, Kiln and Polkachu. They agreed to move the funds only after a passed Cosmos Hub governance proposal gives them a mandate. This proposal is that mandate.

## Mandate

If this proposal passes, the signers of `cosmos1z8pq5cn7tdrwwzlwm0e44fgq07e43ner6vph64` are authorized to:

1. Send the multisig's full `uatom` balance, less network fees, to `neutron1yr29fd7uzdjp2jsq8hrta8mvyd6ex7vumn0shy`.
2. Use a standard ICS-20 `MsgTransfer` from the Hub over `channel-569` (Neutron `channel-1`), with an empty memo and a timeout long enough to cover a relayer outage. On Neutron the ATOM arrives as `ibc/C4CFF46FD6DE35CA4CF4CE031E643C8FDC9BA4B99AE598E9B0ED98FE3A2319F9`.
3. Send a small test transfer first, for example 1 ATOM, and send the rest only after it has arrived.
4. Split the transfer only if a technical limit prevents a single transfer. No ATOM may be held back.
5. Publish the hashes of every transfer and its IBC acknowledgement, and the final balances of both multisigs, in the forum thread.

The signers may not send the ATOM to any other address. A different destination requires a new Hub proposal.

## Why the ATOM goes to Neutron

- It was taken from Drop and Astroport contracts on Neutron and belongs to their users.
- The Hub was not exploited. It only received the stolen funds. Its validators, users and community pool lost nothing, and nothing here asks the Hub to pay for anything.
- The Neutron recovery multisig already holds everything recovered on Neutron: 1,671,302 USDC, 95.2 million NTRN, 370.3 million ASTRO, the stolen dATOM, 14.09 axlWETH and smaller balances. Its signers are 01node, Stake&Relax, Polkachu, Newt Node and Solva. With the ATOM there as well, a single Neutron proposal can return everything.
- The contracts and the affected positions are on Neutron, so Neutron governance is the right place to approve how the funds go back.

## Next step on Neutron

After the ATOM arrives, a Neutron governance proposal will be submitted to return all recovered funds, the ATOM included, to the original contracts they were taken from. Those contracts have been back on their original code and admins since Neutron's recovery release on 25 September, so users can then withdraw through the original Drop and Astroport interfaces. The Neutron multisig signers follow the same rule as the Hub signers: no transfer without a passed Neutron governance proposal. Until then the ATOM stays in the Neutron recovery multisig.

## What this proposal does not do

- It does not spend from the community pool or change any Hub parameter or module.
- It does not execute an on-chain message. The signers send the transfer with their own keys.
- It does not decide how the funds are returned on Neutron. Neutron governance decides that.
- It does not cover ATOM that was not recovered, including the roughly 496,000 ATOM sold before the halt and the 168,990 ATOM THORChain refund that reached the attacker after the restart.
- It does not change the multisig's signers or threshold.

## Vote options

- Yes: move the recovered ATOM to the Neutron recovery multisig as described.
- No: keep the ATOM in the Hub recovery multisig until a different proposal passes.
- No with veto: reject the proposal as spam or as a violation of the Hub's values, and burn the deposit.
- Abstain: count toward quorum without taking a side.

## Links

- Forum discussion: https://forum.cosmos.network/t/discussion-move-the-1-227-121-atom-recovered-after-the-neutron-exploit-to-the-neutron-recovery-multisig
- Neutron incident post-mortem: https://x.com/i/status/2104924316357841306
- Hub halt, restart and recovery multisig: https://forum.cosmos.network/t/hub-weekly-update-17-september-24-2026/17364

proposals.title: ATOM Refund & Justice Bounty
proposals.summary:
1.2M ATOM Refund and 500K ATOM Justice Bounty

## Background

On September 22-23 Cosmos Hub reps coordinated validators to unjustifiably steal 1.2M ATOM from cosmos1dd25c4sshelrpfs0433apg24c5phrhk8m96c4n (ch_user)

Even though the source of these ATOMs should not be Cosmos Hub's problem; here is background:

ch_user conducted series of fair actions with accordance to independent chain governance outside of Cosmos Hub authority.

All actions followed the formal protocol:

1. Governance vote created
2. Community voted
3. Proposal passed

But then:

4. Cosmos hub freezes the chain and steals the balance from ch_user

## Community opinion

Why Cosmos Hub has authority over any user funds?

Shouldn't a decentralized governed system follow rules community has agreed on when chose to participate in Cosmos Hub in the first place?

If the rules can be thrown out whenever someone feels like it, what's the point of having rules at all?

## Proposal description

- Refund 1,221,120 ATOM to ch_user
    - If the liquidity and selling pressure is a concern: ch_user offers a voluntary staking lockup of 1,200,000 ATOM for 2 years, ending October 1, 2028.
- 500,000 ATOM Justice Bounty to all voters who vote "YES" in this proposal
    - 500,000 ATOM will be distributed to voters who voted "YES" proportionally to staking weight.
    - Over the course of 6 months
    - With a cap per voting party of 5,000 ATOM

## Closing thoughts

Decentralized Governed Hub shouldn't be a dictatorship. Otherwise, why governance token ATOM is needed?

If someone in the community or inside Cosmos Hub thinks it is fair to freeze and block any user - they should also need to submit a proposal for the community to vote.

If we wanted one party controlling everything without our consent, we wouldn't be here. We'd be... well, somewhere with a very different political system.

This is Cosmos Hub's chance to prove it actually believes in decentralization, not just talk about it.

Vote YES to fix this mess and stand up for community governance.

proposals.metadata: ATOM Integration & Listing on Paxos’ Regulated Brokerage Infrastructure
proposals.title: ATOM Integration & Listing on Paxos’ Regulated Brokerage Infrastructure
proposals.summary:
**Author**: Paxos

**Target Recipient**: Paxos Trust Company, N.A.

**Requested Amount**: 300,740 USDC

**Payment Terms**: Settlement Upon vote-passage

**Target Launch Date**: September 18

## 1. Executive Summary
This proposal requests a one-time Community Treasury Spend of **300,740 USDC** from the Cosmos Hub Treasury to complete the technical integration, liquidity onboarding, and institutional listing of ATOM on the **Paxos Enterprise Brokerage and Custody Platform**.

ATOM has successfully cleared Paxos’s standard risk review (**Status: Greenlit**). The Cosmos team and Paxos have been engaged for the last couple of months to scope this partnership and are excited to bring this to the DAO for decision. Technical integration and liquidity provisioning are currently underway to meet a targeted platform launch date of **September 18**.

By funding this one-time integration fee, the Cosmos Hub establishes a link into mainstream FinTechs and Traditional financial ecosystems through an OCC-regulated provider. Paxos has agreed to **permanently waive all recurring costs for this integration and maintenance fees** ($0/month), ensuring long-term alignment with the Cosmos Hub Treasury and a single, transparent integration costs.

Paxos has over **600+** globally onboarded Institutions and 10+ different Brokerage clients using Paxos for crypto trading infrastructure, including Charles Schwab, Paypal, Venmo, and Mercado Libre.

## 2. Paxos Institutional Infrastructure & Sole Gateway Positioning
Paxos operates as a premier regulated digital asset infrastructure platform, providing enterprise-grade custody, brokerage, and settlement solutions to top-tier institutional market participants and consumer FinTech platforms.

### Regulatory Rigor & Trust Framework
- **Tier-1 Regulatory Oversight**: Regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC - US National Trust Charter), the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS - Major Payment Institution License)

- **Security & Audits**: Fully compliant with SOC I and SOC II Type II standards.

- **Asset Protection**: Customer assets are held strictly in bankruptcy-remote, segregated accounts backed by digital asset insurance coverage.


### Regulated Infrastructure Gateway

Paxos functions as a regulated **enterprise infrastructure gateway** connecting digital assets directly to leading retail brokerage and FinTech applications. Across our wallet infrastructure (both our QC and MPC offering) Paxos has over $20B+ in AUC. Integrating ATOM onto Paxos infrastructure provides listing capabilities for the asset across Paxos’s distribution network. Public examples include:

- **Interactive Brokers**: 5.3M+ active brokerage accounts

- **CMC**: 2M Global Users

- **Charles Schwab**: 39M brokerage accounts


### Compliance Notice:

**Infrastructure Enablement Model**: This proposal funds the technical enablement, compliance framework, and liquidity gateway on Paxos. Once ATOM is active on Paxos’ core platform, each individual brokerage client retains sole discretion over if, when, and how they choose to turn on ATOM trading and custody for their respective user bases, in accordance with their internal product roadmaps, regional regulatory approvals, and business priorities.

We plan to update the forum quarterly in the first year regarding progress here.

### Continued Partnership: Institutional Staking Offering

Following the initial launch of ATOM custody and trading infrastructure, Paxos will plan to add **Institutional Staking Offering** on the roadmap. Paxos is currently engaged with several partners here to bring:

- **Native Yield Distribution**: Enables enterprise partners and institutional custody clients to participate in Cosmos Hub staking directly through Paxos infrastructure.

- **Recurring Alignment**: Drives long-term staking participation, enhances network security, and establishes a recurring yield mechanism for enterprise capital deployed within the Paxos ecosystem.

## 3. Go-To-Market & Strategic Marketing Execution
To maximize institutional visibility and partner uptake upon launch, Cosmos Labs and Paxos will execute a co-coordinated Go-To-Market strategy:

1. **Enterprise Asset 1-Pager and Co-Branded Collateral**: Publication of an institutional-grade ATOM product sheet and asset overview tailored specifically for decision-makers at Paxos enterprise partner firms highlighting ATOM’s utility and economic model.

2. **Official Custody Announcement**: Joint press release led by Cosmos Labs with Paxos’ support and amplification, and formal announcement broadcast across Paxos’ client channels.

3. **Multi-Phase Social Campaign**: A structured marketing campaign covering:

- Phase 1: “Plan to List” infrastructure announcement.

- Phase 2: Official launch date and custody activation.

- Phase 3: Custody milestones and institutional integration updates.

4. **Direct Client Engagement**: Direct outreach by Paxos product and relationship management teams to engage key institutional and brokerage partners on ATOM enablement options.

5. **Additional Opportunities**: Paxos regularly partners with customers, asset issuers, chain ecosystems and more on additional content, speaking events, webinars and more. This partnership opens the opportunity for follow-on content, case studies and more as adoption through Paxos scales.

## 4. Spend Execution & Treasury Settlement Mechanics
Upon successful passage of this governance proposal, $300,740 USDC will be disbursed from the Cosmos Hub Community Pool to the designated Paxos settlement address.

### Settlement Terms Summary
- **Amount**: 300,740 USDC (represented as 6-decimal Noble USDC IBC token on the Cosmos Hub).

- **Disbursement Conditions**: Funds released directly to Paxos Trust Company following governance approval.

- **Fee Structure**: One-time payment covering all integration, legal, regulatory clearance, and technical provisioning. Zero recurring monthly maintenance fees.

Forum post and discussion: https://forum.cosmos.network/t/atom-integration-listing-on-paxos-regulated-brokerage-infrastructure-proposal-community-treasury-spend/17276

proposals.title: Gaia v28.0.0 Upgrade
proposals.summary:
# Background

The Gaia `v28.0.0` upgrade removes Interchain Security (ICS) from the Cosmos Hub. 

The following will happen as part of this upgrade:

1. The `max_validators` parameter in the staking module will be updated to match the `max_provider_consensus_validators` parameter in the provider module.
2. All bonded validators that are ranked below the new  `max_validator` threshold at the time of the upgrade will be set to unbonding. They will not be jailed or slashed.
3. All tokens in the consumer rewards pool account will be transferred to the community pool, and the consumer rewards pool will be blocked from receiving any additional tokens.
4. All pending VSCPackets will be deleted.
5. All `provider` port IBC channels will be closed.

The upgrade handler will transfer the full remaining balance of the legacy `ConsumerRewardsPool` module account to the community pool. These legacy consumer-chain rewards would otherwise be lost because these are denoms that have been "stuck" in the consumer rewards pool account (they were never registered in a distribution allowlist). Moving them to the community pool preserves the balances, but does not distribute them to validators or delegators. Validators or other independent community members can calculate historical allocations and submit a separate governance proposal if they choose.

Additionally, any queries for ICS messages will now return empty stubs instead of historical data.

If the proposal passes, validators will be required to update the Cosmos Hub binary at the specified upgrade height.

# Release Details

- The release can be found [here](https://github.com/cosmos/gaia/releases/tag/v28.0.0).
- The changelog can be found [here](https://github.com/cosmos/gaia/blob/v28.0.0/CHANGELOG.md).

**This upgrade is state-breaking and mandatory once the on-chain vote passes and the upgrade height is reached.**

# Governance votes

- This proposal has a voting period of **SEVEN DAYS**.
- If the proposal passes, validators will be required to update the Cosmos Hub binary at the specified upgrade height.

The following items summarize the voting options and what it means for this proposal:

YES - You agree that the Cosmos Hub should be updated with this release.

NO - You disagree that the Cosmos Hub should be updated with this release.

NO WITH VETO - A ‘NoWithVeto’ vote indicates a proposal either (1) is deemed to be spam, i.e., irrelevant to Cosmos Hub, (2) disproportionately infringes on minority interests, or (3) violates or encourages violation of the rules of engagement as currently set out by Cosmos Hub governance. If the number of ‘NoWithVeto’ votes is greater than a third of total votes, the proposal is rejected and the deposits are burned.

ABSTAIN - You wish to contribute to the quorum but you formally decline to vote either for or against the proposal.

proposals.title: Fund Hypha to operate the Hub's public testnet program for 2026/2027
proposals.summary:
## Summary

This proposal requests 202,320 USDC to fund one year of work (August 1, 2026 - July 31, 2027) at a monthly flat rate of 16,860 to cover stewardship and maintenance of the Hub's persistent testnet. This flat rate would be withdrawn in USDC from the community pool and held in a Hypha-controlled wallet to be invoiced ahead of each month covered by the funding proposal.

This scope of work includes organizing and running testnet events, reporting validator participation to the Interchain Foundation for the delegations program, and running and administering testnet infrastructure such as snapshots and faucets. It also includes necessary coordination with Cosmos Labs around Gaia release readiness, upgrade rehearsals, testnet-to-mainnet planning, and information transfer for the purposes of reporting and accountability.

Gaia development and maintenance, verification and validation testing, QA, incident response, and mainnet coordination and upgrade monitoring are explicitly **not-in-scope** for this proposal.

## Additional details
* Full proposal text with changelog and discussion on the forum [here](https://forum.cosmos.network/t/last-call-fund-hypha-to-operate-the-hubs-public-testnet-program-for-2026-2027/17033).

## Governance votes and outcomes

**The following items summarize the voting options and what it means for this proposal:**

- **YES:** You agree to fund the Hub testnets team at Hypha Worker Co-operative with a 202k USDC budget for continued stewardship of the Hub's public testnet over the period of August 1, 2026 - July 31, 2027. A 'YES' outcome will immediately release 202k USDC to the specified wallet (`TBD`).
- **NO:** You do not agree to fund the Hub testnets team at Hypha Worker Co-operative based on the terms of this proposal.
- **NO WITH VETO:** A 'NoWithVeto' vote indicates a proposal either (1) is deemed to be spam, i.e., irrelevant to Cosmos Hub, (2) disproportionately infringes on minority interests, or (3) violates or encourages violation of the rules of engagement as currently set out by Cosmos Hub governance. If the number of 'NoWithVeto' votes is greater than a third of total votes, the proposal is rejected and the deposits are burned.
- **ABSTAIN:** You wish to contribute to the quorum but you formally decline to vote either for or against the proposal.

## Hypha's past work on the Hub

Hypha has been a core contributing team on the Cosmos Hub since 2022 with a focus on the Hub's persistent testnet. Our work over the past four years has comprised:

- Weekly or biweekly validator training on new Gaia releases and features released as part of Interchain Security
- Establishing the Testnet Incentives Program to compensate validators for their contributions to the Hub's live testnet (funded at one point or another by AADAO, ICF, and the ICF delegations program)
- Mainnet coordination of upgrades via governance, via manual halt height, and via emergency binary swaps
- Maintenance and dependency bumps for Gaia
- Integration of features requested directly by the community, such as the tokenfactory module
- Deprecation of Interchain Security
- Major upgrade testing and de-risking for all Gaia releases through local testnets, devnets, and public Hub testnets

## Scope of proposed work

### Training Ground
- Designing and running weekly events that walk validators through new features and upgrade paths
- Providing direct support and troubleshooting to node operators
- Establishing and reinforcing operational best practices across the validator set
- Tracking performance and reporting points to ICF on a regular schedule

### Rehearsal Environment
- Coordinating upgrade rehearsals with the Cosmos Labs mainnet team, collecting validator feedback, and reporting any findings to Cosmos Labs or the relevant upstream maintainer to support testnet-to-mainnet pushes
- Documenting resource requirements, timing considerations, and any operational edge cases surfaced during testing
- Identifying compatibility issues with third-party tooling before they affect mainnet

### Development Platform
- Supporting teams running feature or integration testing against live Gaia code
- Maintaining IBC connections to other test networks
- Assisting less technical participants in learning to interact with the Hub, including governance proposal testing

## Work not in-scope
Cosmos Labs' renewed focus on the Hub means that Hypha will be transitioning many pieces of work and will no longer be responsible for the following items which were included in our 2025/2026 contracts (both with the Hub community and Cosmos Labs directly):

- Gaia codebase development and maintenance
- Release and upgrade testing
- Mainnet coordination and upgrade monitoring
- Hub incident response

## Budget and logistics

This proposal asks for a budget of 202,320 USDC, to be invoiced monthly at 16,860 USDC. Our calculations for this monthly rate are given below.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Baseline monthly labour | 45 hours |
| "Busy month" padding | + 18 hours |
| Effective billed hours | = 63 hours |
| Hourly consultancy rate | 220 USD |
| Labour subtotal | 13,860 USD |
| Infrastructure costs | + 3,000 USD |
| Monthly flat rate | = 16,860 USD |
| **Annual total** | **202,320 USD** |

1. A flat rate means that if we work more or less than the effective billed hours, we are paid the same amount regardless. We think this is the appropriate structure for a deliverables-based contract as it incentivizes the contractor (Hypha) to work efficiently rather than inflate our hours.
2. Hypha is a software consultancy, with operating costs. Our consultancy rate is inclusive of our operating costs and profit margin.

The community pool currently contains roughly 1 million USDC, so this proposal will directly request USDC to avoid the need for any buffer and liquidation logistics. If the proposal passes, this amount would be transferred from the community pool into a Hypha-controlled wallet and the team will invoice this wallet in advance every month for the duration of the proposal's funding period.

If the community puts up and passes a proposal instructing Hypha to suspend our work on the testnet, we will immediately stop our work, provide transition materials to a successor team specified to the community, and return any un-invoiced funds to the community pool.
